prompt:
TESSERA STYLE SHEET
1. Modern editorial paper collage: bold magazine composition, refined 2D motion design, photographed flat under soft room light.
2. One flat block-colour paper ground fills the frame: deep magenta. The ground is a single unbroken colour.
3. Subjects are black-and-white halftone photographic cutouts with rough white torn-paper edges: objects, machines, buildings, maps, coins, screens, vehicles, anonymous paper hands. Every cutout is a plain, unmarked object: calendar pages, documents, coins, screens and vehicles are blank and unprinted, with no lettering, numerals, symbols, liveries or marks on them.
4. Diagram elements are flat matte paper shapes and ribbons in cream, black, pale yellow, or the ground's contrasting colour, with real paper texture, print dots and small pieces of tape.
5. One consistent light from the upper left; each paper layer casts a small soft shadow.
6. Every surface is matte printed paper reflecting only the room light: cutouts, chips, ribbons and ground all read as photographed paper, with the same flat finish edge to edge. No glow, neon, bloom or halo anywhere.
7. Layout: the headline chip owns the upper third of the frame and stays uncovered; subjects and diagrams occupy the lower two-thirds. When the frame opens on a previous composition, its elements slide off or are covered in the first second and the new headline lands on clear ground.
8. Headline typography: one extra-bold sans-serif in black or cream, printed on a cream or black paper chip, large, with safe margins. Letterforms are accurate, complete and stable from the frame they appear in; the chip is printed once and does not redraw.
9. Motion: elements enter fast with slight overshoot and a stable landing, then hold a clear reading window; one strongest focus at a time; the camera is locked; movement starts on the first frame and a small loop continues at the end; no empty frames.
10. 16:9, exactly 5 seconds, one composition, at most one crisp cut.
11. Identity anchor: rough white torn edges on every cutout; small paper shadow from the upper-left light.

BEAT
Ground: deep magenta.
Subjects: a torn-paper arrow; paper coins.
Opens on the row of buildings, carried over from the previous shot, which transforms as the action begins.
Action: The previous chip flips off as the buildings collapse into paper coins; a torn-paper arrow enters and points down at them.
Ends holding on the down arrow.
Headline printed on a paper chip: "$1.16".

ON-SCREEN TEXT: "$1.16". This string is printed complete and correct from its first visible frame and never changes. It is the only lettering in the frame.

AUDIO: No voice, no speech, no dialogue, no lyrics. Light paper-slap and tape sound effects only; no music.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] This is a modern editorial paper collage in a cinematic 2D motion design style, photographed as a flat lay under soft, consistent room light coming from the upper left. <Picture 1> serves as the first frame, showing a light-blue paper ground with a cream-colored paper chip at the top bearing the black text "BANKS & FUNDS" and a row of black-and-white halftone photographic cutouts of neoclassical buildings below, all featuring rough white torn-paper edges and casting small, soft shadows. Immediately, the scene transforms: the blue ground is instantly covered by a single, unbroken block of deep magenta matte paper. The cream chip with "BANKS & FUNDS" flips upward and slides off the frame rapidly with a slight overshoot. Simultaneously, the halftone buildings collapse downward, their forms splintering and rearranging into a scattered pile of black-and-white halftone paper coins. These coins are plain and unmarked, with no numerals or symbols. A new cream-colored paper chip enters from the top, landing firmly in the upper third of the frame; it features the bold, black, extra-bold sans-serif text "$1.16", which remains stable, clean, and legible. A black-and-white halftone paper arrow with rough white torn edges slides in quickly from the right, pointing directly downward at the pile of paper coins. The camera remains a Static Shot throughout. By the end of the 5-second duration, the composition holds on the "$1.16" headline and the downward-pointing arrow over the coins, with all elements exhibiting a matte printed paper texture and subtle paper shadows.

overall_soundscape: The audio consists of crisp, tactile foley sounds. There are sharp, light paper-slap sounds as the chips flip and land, accompanied by the distinct, sticky sound of adhesive tape being pressed down. A soft, rustling shuffle is heard as the paper buildings collapse into coins.
